clips.send: Opium War and Treaty of Nanjing. 1840—1842. The beginning of China’s modern history. June 1839: the official Lin Zexu (林则徐 Lín Zéxú) destroyed confiscated opium on the beach at Humen (虎门 Hǔmén), near Guangzhou — a heavy blow to opium smuggling. June 1840: using the Humen opium destruction as an excuse, Britain launched the Opium War. August 1842: the Qing government was forced to sign the Treaty of Nanjing: cede Hong Kong Island to Britain; pay 21 million silver dollars; open Guangzhou, Xiamen, Fuzhou, Ningbo and Shanghai as treaty ports; tariffs on British goods had to be agreed with Britain. Impact: China began to sink into a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society. The Opium War marks the start of China’s modern history.

clips.send: Self-Strengthening Movement. 1860s—1890s. Learning Western technology: “self-strengthening” (自强 zìqiáng) and “seeking wealth” (求富 qiúfù). Leaders: Prince Gong (Yixin) at court; Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang, Zuo Zongtang and Zhang Zhidong in the provinces. Guiding idea: “Chinese learning as the foundation, Western learning for practical use.”. Early stage, slogan “self-strengthening”: military industries such as the Anqing Arsenal, the Jiangnan Arsenal and the Fuzhou Navy Yard. Later stage, slogan “seeking wealth”: civilian industries such as the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company and the Hanyang Iron Works; also new navies such as the Beiyang Fleet, new-style schools and students sent abroad. The Beiyang Fleet’s total defeat in the Sino-Japanese War marked its failure, but it brought in Western technology and China’s first modern enterprises — it is seen as the start of China’s modernisation.

clips.send: Hundred Days’ Reform. 1898. Reformists tried to build a constitutional monarchy. 1895: Kang Youwei and the provincial graduates in Beijing for the exam petitioned the emperor — the “Gongche Petition” (公车上书 gōngchē shàngshū). 11 June 1898: Emperor Guangxu issued the edict “Defining the State Policy” and launched the reform. Measures: reform government offices and appoint reformers; encourage private mines and factories; open new schools, drop the “eight-legged essay” (a rigid essay form used in the old exams), found the Imperial University of Peking; train a new army and navy. 21 September: Empress Dowager Cixi staged a coup and the reform failed; Tan Sitong and the other “Six Gentlemen” were killed. It lasted 103 days. Significance: a patriotic political movement and an ideological enlightenment.

clips.send: 洋务运动。19世纪60—90年代。学习西方先进技术：“自强”“求富”。代表人物：中央有奕䜣，地方有曾国藩、李鸿章、左宗棠、张之洞等。指导思想：“中学为体，西学为用”。前期以“自强”为口号，创办军事工业，如安庆内军械所、江南制造总局、福州船政局。后期以“求富”为口号，创办民用工业，如轮船招商局、汉阳铁厂；还筹划海防，建立北洋水师等新式海军，创办新式学堂，派遣留学生。甲午战争中北洋舰队全军覆没，标志着洋务运动失败；但它引进了西方先进技术，使中国出现了第一批近代企业，被视为中国近代化的开端。

clips.send: 新文化运动。1915年起。一场思想解放运动。1915年，陈独秀在上海创办《青年杂志》（第二卷起改名《新青年》），新文化运动兴起。代表人物：陈独秀、李大钊、鲁迅、胡适等；北京大学成为运动的中心之一。主要内容：提倡民主，反对专制；提倡科学，反对愚昧；提倡新道德，反对旧道德；提倡新文学，反对旧文学。胡适发表《文学改良刍议》；鲁迅发表第一篇白话小说《狂人日记》。后期，李大钊等宣传马克思主义；运动促进了思想解放，为马克思主义在中国的传播创造了条件。
